newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: SLOVAK CEN BANK SETS TWO REV REPO TENDERS FOR THUR.
newsitem.headline: SLOVAK CEN BANK SETS TWO REV REPO TENDERS FOR THUR.

text.p: The National Bank of Slovakia (NBS) on Thursday said it had set two securities reverse repurchase tenders for 10 a.m. (0900 GMT), offering to sterilise an unspecified volume of market liquidity.
The NBS said in a statement that the operations would consist of a one-day reverse repo tender, as well as a seven-day reverse repo tender.
The NBS added the American-style tenders would have no fixed minimum rate.
In the NBS's one-day reverse repo tender on Wednesday, the average rate rose to 17.4 percent, after 17.03 percent in the previous reverse repo tender of a similar maturity on Tuesday.
In the seven-day tender on Wednesday, the first at such a maturity this year, the average rate was 17.00 percent.

According to official NBS figures, the Slovak banking sector has a liquidity surplus, with banks' minimum reserve demands fulfilled at 102.68 percent as of Wednesday, after being at 102.75 percent the previous day.
